description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a 2D Designer based in Switzerland. Join a creative, community-driven digital environment where immersive social experiences, virtual worlds, and user-generated content come together. As a 2D Designer, you will create polished, engaging visuals across storefronts, marketing campaigns, in-app promotions, and virtual environments. Your work will help showcase digital products, strengthen visual storytelling, and enhance the experience of users exploring a vibrant social VR platform. You will design everything from product thumbnails and promotional banners to social media graphics, event signage, and in-world textures. The role requires a versatile creative approach, combining strong visual design skills with an understanding of how graphics perform across different sizes, formats, and interfaces. Working collaboratively with a distributed team, you will respond to feedback, adapt to evolving priorities, and deliver high-quality assets within established brand guidelines. This is an excellent opportunity for a resourceful designer who enjoys variety, values attention to detail, and wants to contribute to a growing digital community through impactful visual communication. Accountabilities Storefront design: Create compelling thumbnails and graphics for digital store listings, ensuring products are visually appealing, easy to understand, and recognizable at small sizes. Bundle graphics and visual identity: Design promotional graphics for product bundles, clearly communicating included items while maintaining strong visual appeal. Develop distinct themes for each bundle, including backgrounds, navigation icons, and mobile-friendly variations that remain consistent with the overall storefront identity. Marketing and promotional assets: Produce engaging social media posts, announcement graphics, blog headers, and other marketing materials that support campaigns, product updates, and community initiatives. Video graphics: Design static visual assets for video content, including title cards, overlays, and end screens, ensuring consistency with established branding and communication objectives. Platform-specific creative production: Prepare and export graphics for distribution platforms such as Steam and Meta, adapting each asset to the relevant dimensions, file formats, and technical specifications. In-app visual design: Create banners for events and promotions, notification graphics, and other in-app visuals that integrate naturally with the user interface and remain legible at smaller display sizes. In-world artwork: Develop signage, posters, textures, and other 2D assets used within virtual worlds, helping create visually engaging and immersive user experiences. Brand consistency and creative execution: Work within established visual guidelines while giving individual assets their own distinctive character, ensuring a cohesive yet varied visual identity across different touchpoints. Multi-format adaptation: Optimize designs for different screen sizes, layouts, and contexts, including mobile devices, storefronts, social channels, and in-app interfaces. Feedback and iteration: Collaborate with stakeholders, incorporate feedback efficiently, and refine designs through quick review cycles while adapting to changing priorities and deadlines. Asset organization and delivery: Maintain clean, well-organized working files, consistent naming conventions, and properly layered source documents to support efficient collaboration and future updates. Requirements A strong portfolio demonstrating a range of 2D design work, ideally including marketing graphics, user interface assets, storefront visuals, or digital product promotions. Proven experience creating graphics for multiple formats and display sizes, particularly thumbnails, icons, banners, and mobile layouts. Strong proficiency in industry-standard design tools such as Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, Figma, or comparable creative software. A solid understanding of visual hierarchy, typography, composition, color, and branding, with the ability to create polished, high-impact graphics for different audiences and contexts. Experience working within an existing brand identity while developing creative variations that give individual campaigns, products, or collections a distinctive look. Familiarity with preparing and exporting assets according to platform-specific technical requirements, including file formats, dimensions, and resolution specifications. The ability to design for small-scale displays, ensuring that graphics remain clear, legible, and visually effective when viewed within compact interfaces. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to understand creative briefs, respond constructively to feedback, and work through rapid revision cycles. Flexibility and adaptability when managing changing priorities, multiple types of creative deliverables, and short turnaround times. Excellent file management practices, including organized project folders, consistent naming conventions, and properly layered, editable source files. A detail-oriented approach and a commitment to maintaining high visual quality and consistency across all deliverables. The ability to work independently in a remote environment while coordinating effectively with a distributed creative team. Nice to have Familiarity with social VR platforms, virtual communities, or user-generated virtual environments. Experience creating textures or other 2D assets for real-time 3D applications, particularly projects built with Unity. An understanding of how visual assets contribute to digital storefront conversion, community engagement, and immersive user experiences. Experience supporting digital product launches, online campaigns, or event-based promotional activities. Benefits Fully remote work: Work remotely from Anywhere, with flexibility to organize your work within agreed project timelines and deliverables. Part-time engagement: A contract opportunity suited to a designer seeking a flexible, project-based workload. Creative variety: Work across storefront graphics, marketing campaigns, social media, in-app promotions, and virtual-world artwork. Portfolio development: Build a diverse body of work spanning digital product design, marketing communication, interface graphics, and immersive environments. Creative ownership: Contribute original ideas and distinctive visual treatments while working within an established brand identity. Collaborative environment: Work with a creative, distributed team that values collaboration, feedback, and contributions from different perspectives. Fast-paced creative experience: Develop your ability to deliver polished assets through iterative design processes and changing project priorities. Exposure to social VR: Gain experience creating visual assets for a platform centered on virtual worlds, digital communities, and user-generated experiences. Pourquoi être AE Mid & Up Market chez Doctrine ? Vendre la Legal Tech la plus performante du marché, qui innove en permanence et est en avance de phase sur les sujets d'IA Générative ; S’appuyer sur des équipes Ops et Marketing bien staffées et de haut niveau, au service de la performance des Sales au quotidien ; Pouvoir évoluer dans une équipe avec des profils divers, qui met l'accent sur la formation et l’accompagnement dès le premier jour ; Bénéficier d'un package attractif comprenant un variable déplafonné. Les missions 🛠 Tu es amené.e à porter le cycle de vente de A à Z : dans une démarche d'acquisition, tu prospectes sur le parc qui t’es confié, qualifies le besoin des comptes, montres la valeur de l’outil au travers de démonstrations, construis des offre financières adaptées, négocies & signes un maximum de deals. Tu adresses principalement ces comptes en outbound, avec un approche multi-interlocuteurs ; tu optimises la vélocité commerciale en équilibrant vitesse d’exécution et taux de transformation. Tu travailles main dans la main avec l’équipe étendue de Doctrine pour générer des opportunités business : tu te coordonnes au quotidien avec les BDR et les CSM/AM qui contribueront directement à ton activité, et tu pourras t’appuyer sur les équipes Ops, Marketing et Product pour accélérer la croissance sur ton segment. Le profil idéal 👀 Tu as une expérience de vente complexe avec des profils exécutifs (C-Level) d’au moins 3 ans, idéalement dans la vente de logiciels SaaS. Tu maitrises à la perfection des méthodologies de vente telles que MEDDIC, qui te permettent d’établir des prévisions précises et à jour de ton business chaque mois. Tu t'intéresses aux technologies liées à l'intelligence artificielle générative Une formation/expérience juridique confirmée est appréciée mais non un prérequis. La connaissance de Salesforce est un atout. Tu es tenace, mets les excuses au placard et as un fort attrait pour le résultat ; tu es motivé.e par une perspective de variable déplafonné. Tu es un.e véritable chasseur.se, passionné.e de prospection : tu sais faire preuve de résilience, d’écoute, et de conviction, et tu sais prioriser avec focus. Tu as une forte culture du feedback et souhaites progresser sans cesse. Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝 Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert. Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides. Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien. Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc. Nos valeurs 🤝 Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses. Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur. Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership. Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser. Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques. Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️ 🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine. 🌴 Une politique de congés flexibles 🌱 Des opportunités concrètes de mobilité interne 🏄‍♂️ Des évènements collectifs réguliers 📚 Un vrai accent sur la formation individuelle et collective, avec un budget annuel de 750€ pour toute formation en lien avec ton poste - et des formations en équipe ou pour toute l'entreprise 🏋️‍♀️ Un abonnement Gymlib pour les activités sportives et bien-être 🧘 Un accès gratuit à la plateforme d'accompagnement à la santé mentale Moka.care et un accompagnement individuel allant jusqu’à 6 séances par an 👩‍⚕️ Une assurance santé avec Alan 🍱 🚲 Une carte Swile pour tes tickets restaurants et ton forfait mobilité durable (66,60 euros par mois) 💡 Des réductions et avantages négociés grâce à notre CSE via la plateforme Happypal 🍏 Un équipement de travail neuf chez Apple Notre processus de recrutement 🚀 Un premier échange de 30 min avec l’un.e de nos Talent Acquisition Manager pour bien comprendre ton projet professionnel et te présenter ce qu'on construit chez Doctrine Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions. Alan is looking for a Global Brand Event Manager to turn events into a distinctive, scalable expression of the Alan brand. You will own Alan’s yearly flagship event, building on the success of Alan 10, and help make it an even stronger moment for brand, community, customers, prospects, partners, and the wider healthcare ecosystem. Beyond the flagship event, you will build the operating system that enables commercial and local teams to run high-quality events repeatedly and consistently. It is a senior individual-contributor role that owns the global event system and makes other teams more autonomous and effective. You will lead the global strategy and execution of Alan’s major Brand events, while owning the execution of local Brand events in France. You will create the playbooks, standards, templates, and measurement frameworks that allow teams across markets to deliver high-quality events without reinventing the wheel each time. You will also contribute to the Brand team’s global community-event strategy, identifying the formats and moments that can make Alan more visible, credible, and memorable to the communities we want to influence. You’ll equip local teams with the right local approach and assets, and support them as they adapt and run events in their markets. Main responsibilities Own Alan’s yearly flagship event Participate in the definition of the event’s purpose, audience, positioning, narrative, and success criteria. Build the event roadmap, budget, and production plan. Manage agencies, venues, suppliers, speakers, partners, and internal stakeholders. Coordinate content, creative, production, guest management, press, influencers, Sales, and local market teams. Design a high-quality guest experience before, during, and after the event. Connect invitations, registration, CRM tracking, attendance, and follow-up. Run rehearsals, speaker preparation, run-of-show management, and on-site execution. Build Alan’s recurring event playbook Define the main event formats and their intended purposes, such as owned events, executive dinners, round tables, speaking opportunities, trade shows, and partner events. Create practical templates for briefs, timelines, budgets, approvals, execution, production, and follow-up. Help define the role of commercial teams before, during, and after the event. Create reusable content, event assets, checklists, and quality standards. Support local teams on local events Help local teams choose the right format and define the desired outcome. Review briefs and plans, provide feedback, and raise the quality bar. Identify successful local formats that could be scaled globally. Help shape and execute Alan’s community-event strategy Contribute with the Brand team to the Community building strategy Design recurring event franchises and formats. Build partnerships with relevant organizations, experts, customers, and opinion leaders. Run test-and-learn initiatives that can start locally and scale globally. Profile & Competencies We are looking for someone who has: At least 5 years of experience delivering events end to end, ideally in a Brand, B2B marketing or agency environment. A track record of creating original event concepts and formats, not only executing a brief. Strong editorial judgement: the right angle, speakers and content to make an event memorable. Brand creativity: a clear point of view on how an event expresses a brand. Experience running complex events with multiple stakeholders, agencies, suppliers and speakers (including profiles with special logistics and security needs). Strong production skills: planning, budgeting, vendor and risk management, rehearsals and on-site delivery. Experience building repeatable processes, playbooks or templates. A strong understanding of how events drive brand, community and commercial outcomes, and comfort with CRM, registration, lead capture and follow-up. description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people". The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build. Why we're hiring Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it. Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work. We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff. About the role You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push. You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions. What you'll actually do Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself. Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more. Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates. Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time. Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet. Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too. Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating. What this role isn't An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job. A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more. A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked. A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes. A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above. What success looks like In your first 90 days: The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so. Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved. You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted. Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week. At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more. We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined. After a year: You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to. The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well. Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you. Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings. About you You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something. You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it. You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company. You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise. AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once. You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails. You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does. You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm. Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway. Bonus points: You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD. You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end. You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance). You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it. You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting. How you will grow This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year. Remuneration and benefits Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together. An environment where you can do your best work: 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier) 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally) 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine ☕ Very good coffee 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots! ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays) 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that. The environment Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership. We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation. If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: We are currently looking for an experienced professional to join an acute care hospital in the Zurich Oberland as Head of Urology. In this role, you will assume overall medical, financial, and personnel responsibility for the urology department, which handles approximately 850 inpatient admissions per year, and play a key role in shaping the future of urology in the region. Responsibilities Assume overall responsibility for the urology department in terms of medical care, financial performance, and personnel management. Strengthen and further develop key specialisations, including uro-oncology with prostatectomy and nephrectomy, complex endourology, robotic surgery, transurethral therapies, continence, and sexology. Ensure high standards of treatment quality and provide attractive training and professional development opportunities in collaboration with three senior physicians and affiliated physicians. Lead a service-oriented, interprofessional department while ensuring efficient use of resources. Maintain and expand regional partnerships with referring physicians, independent practitioners, and partner hospitals. Support the department management in further developing the hospital's surgical specialties. Requirements & Qualifications Specialist qualification in Urology and a Swiss subspecialty qualification in Uro-Oncology. Several years of clinical experience, with broad specialist knowledge and extensive surgical expertise. A confident, integrative leadership personality with strong interpersonal skills when dealing with employees, referring physicians, and partners. An understanding of interdisciplinary and interprofessional collaboration on an equal footing, as well as basic business and financial knowledge. Enthusiasm for training and mentoring younger colleagues. Experience initiating, leading, and implementing projects. Benefits & Culture A high degree of professional autonomy and the opportunity to further develop and establish urology as a key specialty in the region. A cantonal service mandate for prostatectomies and nephrectomies. Modern infrastructure and state-of-the-art surgical equipment. The opportunity to expand existing areas of specialisation and establish new ones together with the team. Well-established interdisciplinary collaboration and short decision-making processes. A teaching hospital affiliated with the University of Zurich, a central location near the train station, and either a ZVV BonusPass public transport benefit or affordable parking options Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

description: Co-Founder | Growth, Community & Partnerships (m/w/d) Standort: München (überwiegend vor Ort) Start: Voraussichtlich Februar/März 2027 Compensation: EXIST Gründungsstipendium, 2.500 € monatlich für Hochschulabsolventen, plus geplante Beteiligung am Unternehmen Über uns Wir sind Pierre-Louis Suckrow und Kerim Anater. Unsere akademischen und beruflichen Hintergründe liegen in Informatik, Design & Computation und Human Computer Interaction. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir eine neue Plattform für die Organisation und Zusammenarbeit in der digitalen Musikproduktion. Unser Produkt soll es ermöglichen, verschiedene Projektstände und ihre Entstehung nachzuvollziehen, frühere Versionen wiederherzustellen und Projekte zwischen unterschiedlichen Produktionsumgebungen auszutauschen. Damit möchten wir mehr Raum für musikalisches Experimentieren schaffen, den organisatorischen Aufwand in kreativen Arbeitsprozessen reduzieren und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Musikschaffenden erleichtern. Ein erster funktionsfähiger Prototyp für Ableton Live existiert bereits. Wir sind Teil des WaveLab Inkubators Batch #7 und im Wintersemester Teil der Munich Music Labs. Aktuell bereiten wir unsere Bewerbung für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor. Zur Ergänzung unserer technischen und produktorientierten Kompetenzen suchen wir ein drittes Gründungsmitglied, das insbesondere die Kommunikation nach außen, den Aufbau von Kontakten und die Entwicklung von Kundenbeziehungen mitgestaltet. Deine Rolle In der kommenden Projektphase stehen die Weiterentwicklung des Produkts, die Validierung mit potenziellen Nutzern und der Aufbau erster Kundenbeziehungen und Partnerschaften im Vordergrund. Wir suchen eine Person, die diese Prozesse begleitet und insbesondere den Austausch mit Menschen außerhalb unseres Teams übernimmt. Mögliche Schwerpunkte sind: Communications & PR: Entwicklung unserer Außenkommunikation, Vermittlung unserer Produktidee und Aufbau von Sichtbarkeit innerhalb der Musikbranche und darüber hinaus. Community Building: Aufbau und Betreuung einer Community aus Musikproduzenten, Musikschaffenden und weiteren potenziellen Nutzern. Partnerships & Networking: Kontaktaufnahme und Beziehungspflege mit Studios, Unternehmen, Branchenakteuren und potenziellen Kooperationspartnern. Customer Discovery & Success: Durchführung von Gesprächen mit potenziellen Nutzern, Begleitung erster Beta User und Pilotprojekte sowie systematische Erfassung von Feedback. Growth & Business Development: Mitentwicklung unserer Go to Market Strategie, Erschließung erster Kundengruppen und Validierung unseres Geschäftsmodells. Die genaue Aufgabenverteilung möchten wir gemeinsam und abhängig von deinen bisherigen Erfahrungen und Interessen entwickeln. Als drittes Gründungsmitglied bist du darüber hinaus an der strategischen und unternehmerischen Entwicklung des Vorhabens beteiligt. Wen wir suchen Wir suchen eine kommunikative und eigenständig arbeitende Person, die gerne mit Menschen in Kontakt tritt und Interesse daran hat, ein technologisches Produkt von der frühen Entwicklung bis zum Markteintritt zu begleiten. Idealerweise bringst du Folgendes mit: Erfahrung in einem kommunikationsorientierten Bereich, beispielsweise PR, Marketing, Community Management, Customer Success, Sales, Account Management oder Business Development. Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen verständlich zu kommunizieren und unterschiedliche Zielgruppen anzusprechen. Freude am Aufbau und an der Pflege von Kontakten und langfristigen Beziehungen. Eigeninitiative, organisatorische Fähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Interesse an digitalen Produkten, Technologie und kreativen Arbeitsprozessen. Interesse an der gemeinsamen Gründung und langfristigen Entwicklung eines Unternehmens. Nice to have, aber keine Voraussetzung: Erfahrung in der Musikindustrie oder Kontakte zu Musikproduzenten, Studios, Labels oder Artists. Erfahrung mit Startups, Software Produkten oder dem Aufbau von Communities. Eigene Erfahrung oder Interesse im Bereich Musikproduktion. Ein bestimmter beruflicher Hintergrund ist für uns nicht ausschlaggebend. Entscheidend sind die Bereitschaft, sich in neue Themen einzuarbeiten, eigenständig Verantwortung zu übernehmen und die fachliche sowie persönliche Ergänzung innerhalb unseres Gründungsteams. EXIST Förderung & Compensation Wir bereiten aktuell unseren Antrag für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor. Das Förderprogramm unterstützt Gründungsteams über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Monaten bei der Entwicklung und Validierung ihres Gründungsvorhabens. Während der Förderung erhält jedes Teammitglied abhängig von der Qualifikation ein monatliches Stipendium: 2.500 € pro Monat mit Hochschulabschluss 3.000 € pro Monat mit Promotion 2.000 € pro Monat mit anerkanntem Berufsabschluss 1.000 € pro Monat als Student oder Studentin Das Stipendium dient der Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts und ist kein reguläres Angestelltengehalt. Die Förderung steht unter dem Vorbehalt der Bewilligung unseres EXIST Antrags. Voraussetzungen für die EXIST Förderung: Ein Hochschulabschluss, der in der Regel nicht länger als fünf Jahre zurückliegt, oder eine andere nach EXIST zulässige Qualifikation. Für eine Person im Gründungsteam sind Ausnahmen möglich. Ein Wohnsitz in Deutschland beziehungsweise die Möglichkeit, während der Förderung in Deutschland zu leben und sich hier anzumelden. Die Bereitschaft, sich während der Förderphase in Vollzeit dem Gründungsvorhaben zu widmen. Weitere Informationen zum Förderprogramm findest du auf der offiziellen EXIST Website. Wir suchen ausdrücklich ein langfristiges Gründungsmitglied und keine befristete Anstellung. Wir streben eine weitgehend gleichberechtigte Beteiligung am zukünftigen Unternehmen an. Die konkrete Ausgestaltung möchten wir gemeinsam besprechen. Zusammenarbeit Wir sind derzeit in München und Berlin ansässig. Für die Gründungsphase möchten wir das Team in München zusammenbringen, um die Produktentwicklung und den Unternehmensaufbau gemeinsam vor Ort voranzutreiben. Daher suchen wir jemanden, der bereits in München lebt oder bereit ist, für die gemeinsame Gründungsphase nach München zu ziehen. Da wir uns noch in einer frühen Entwicklungsphase befinden, sind viele Aspekte der späteren Unternehmensstruktur und Aufgabenverteilung noch offen. Diese möchten wir gemeinsam als Gründungsteam gestalten. Interesse? Wenn du dir vorstellen kannst, unser Gründungsteam zu ergänzen, freuen wir uns über eine kurze Vorstellung und Informationen zu deinem bisherigen Hintergrund. Weitere Informationen zum Produkt, unserer bisherigen Forschung und dem geplanten Gründungsvorhaben teilen wir gerne in einem persönlichen Gespräch. description: Notre mission ⚖️ Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe. Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence. Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée. Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance. Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales. Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction. Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début. Le contexte Nous cherchons un ingénieur fullstack pour nous aider à construire la première plateforme d’intelligence juridique. Tu rejoindras l'équipe Platform dont la mission est la gestion de l’authentification et de la gestion des utilisateurs, de notre architecture logicielle, de la sécurité et de l’infrastructure de nos plateformes ainsi que de l’excellence opérationnelle pour les développeurs. La squad se compose d’ingénieurs fullstack. Notre stack technique Web est basée sur NodeJS, Terraform, NestJS, React & NextJS. Tu peux trouver des détails sur l’ensemble de la stack sur Github https://github.com/DoctrineLegal/#our-tech-stack ! A savoir : il n’est pas nécessaire d’avoir une expérience professionnelle dans le domaine du droit ! Les missions 🛠 Proposer des évolutions de notre architecture logicielle en termes de cadres et d'outils. Participer à leur mise en œuvre. Travailler sur nos différentes plateformes en particulier la maintenance et l'évolution de l'authentification et de l'autorisation (par exemple, le support du SSO), y compris son expérience utilisateur. Dans le but de rendre les équipes autonomes, travailler sur l’automatisation des déploiements des applications à Doctrine. Aider les différentes équipes produit à améliorer leur productivité en travaillant sur l'expérience des développeurs. Participer aux astreintes de la squad pour assurer la disponibilité de doctrine.fr. Effectuer des revues de code et rédiger des tests pour maintenir la qualité au niveau de nos standards. Instrumenter ton code pour qu'il puisse être monitoré en production Contribuer à l'infra as code en utilisant Terraform Être en charge de la mise en place et de la maintenance des systèmes d'information et des systèmes de gestion de l'information. Rédiger de la documentation technique Participer à la diffusion interne et à la consolidation de nos bonnes pratiques ; contribuer à l’élaboration de notre stratégie Engineering. Le profil idéal 👀 Une expérience significative en tant qu'ingénieur Fullstack dans la construction de frontends et d'API, éventuellement avec différents niveaux de séniorité dans le backend et le frontend. Très bonne connaissance de Node.JS, TypeScript, React, ou un autre framework front-end, ainsi que NestJS ou un autre framework côté serveur. Intérêt pour l'infrastructure as code Très bonne connaissance de SQL De l’intérêt pour la qualité du code et pour les bonnes pratiques de développement en général (tests, CI/CD...). Une familiarité avec les processus agiles et orientation produit Un engagement à construire la meilleure expérience utilisateur L’ambition de livrer des applications avec une haute fiabilité et une haute disponibilité Le goût du partage et du feedback pour contribuer à faire progresser tes collègues Les à côtés du poste 👁 Comme tous les ingénieurs de Doctrine, tu participeras à un de nos chapters transverses, en l’espèce le chapter Software engineering. Au sein de ce chapter, tu contribueras à des projets internes pour améliorer nos process et notre vision long-terme. description:

Missions

En tant que Head of B2B & Energy, vous portez le développement de WPP Enterprise Solutions sur les marchés B2B et sur le secteur de l’énergie (énergéticiens, utilities, acteurs de la transition énergétique et de la mobilité). Vous incarnez une posture de vente “architecte” : comprendre des enjeux clients transverses – commerciaux, opérationnels, data, technologiques, réglementaires – et y répondre en orchestrant des équipes pluridisciplinaires. Comme l’ensemble de l’équipe de Business Développement, vous reposez sur un profil hybride dont les 2 piliers sont d’être :

  • Responsable de bout en bout du parcours d’avant-vente et de vente de nos offres et de nos capabilities auprès de clients et prospects,
  • Consultant ou directeur de mission, mobilisant une compréhension fine des enjeux B2B et énergie pour structurer des réponses transverses et activer les bonnes expertises (métier, data, technologique, créative) au sein de WPP Enterprise Solutions et du réseau WPP

Cette hybridation, couplée à une posture “architecte”, est la clé du succès : être à la fois expert de la vente complexe, capable de lire des enjeux clients transverses, et en maîtrise des pans complets du métier du conseil et de l’agence.

Dimension Business :

  • Définit et déploie la stratégie de go-to-market de WPP Enterprise Solutions sur les marchés B2B et le secteur de l’énergie, afin d’en faire l’acteur le plus attractif, singulier et impactant,
  • Construit et anime un plan de comptes ciblé (énergéticiens, utilities, grands comptes B2B) pour maintenir une intensité relationnelle élevée auprès des décideurs, défendre notre positionnement et détecter les opportunités de croissance,
  • Pilote, en posture d’architecte, la construction de propositions adressant des enjeux transverses : cadre la problématique client, structure la réponse et orchestre les Business Units et expertises (data, conseil, technologie, créatif) nécessaires à sa conversion,
  • Met en œuvre, en continue, l’excellence du parcours de vente via les processus et les outils internes à des fins de visibilité, de pilotage et d’animation globale de la démarche commerciale en interne,
  • Sécurise et défend les intérêts économique et contractuel de WPP Enterprise Solutions dans le cadre de la vente et après celle-ci,
  • Assure un suivi régulier des prestations et des relations avec les clients donneur d’ordres et les opérationnels pour s’assurer de l’adéquation de la prestation avec le besoin, et identifier des opportunités de suite ou d’extension de la mission,
  • Contribue au thought leadership de WPP Enterprise Solutions sur les enjeux B2B et énergie (transition énergétique, décarbonation, expérience client B2B, data), via des prises de parole valorisant nos convictions et nos réussites dans une logique de ROI business,
  • Construit et fait vivre un patrimoine de connaissances sur les marchés B2B et le secteur de l’énergie (acteurs, enjeux réglementaires, dynamiques de marché) afin d’accélérer et de fluidifier l’action commerciale,
  • Incarne, diffuse et fait vivre l’excellence commerciale en interne, en particulier auprès de la communauté managériale pour l’inspirer, la faire progresser et développer ses appétences et son niveau d’impact business.

Dimension Conseil :

  • Réalise, seul ou en équipe, des missions de conseil sur les sujets B2B et énergie, afin de maintenir un haut niveau de crédibilité et de légitimité dans la dimension Business,
  • Pilote des missions de conseil, sur l’ensemble des composantes : qualité des livrables, respects des plannings et des engagements, tenue de l’équilibre budgétaire,
  • Fait évoluer son savoir-faire et ses connaissances via une veille continue sur les sujets qui comptent pour nos clients et prospects, mais aussi des formations et sa curiosité,
  • Maîtrise et met en œuvre toute la chaîne de production d’une mission de la prise de commande au recouvrement, pour assurer performance opérationnelle complète,
  • Manage des équipes pluridisciplinaires de consultants dans le cadre des missions, et assure une coordination et une information continue de sa hiérarchie pour permettre un feedback constructif et le développement des compétences,
  • Garantit la capitalisation du savoir et des livrables sur ses missions, et partage des retours d’expérience autant que de besoin.

Profil recherché

  • Vous justifiez de 7 à 15 ans d’expérience, dont un parcours significatif en cabinet conseil (stratégie, transformation ou conseil opérationnel).
  • Vous avez impérativement une expérience des marchés B2B et/ou du secteur de l’énergie (énergéticiens, utilities, transition énergétique).
  • Notre métier consistant à vendre et réaliser des missions mobilisant une grande diversité de compétences (data, conseil, créatif, technologique), vous avez développé une véritable appétence pour la vente “architecte” : savoir lire des enjeux clients transverses et y répondre en mobilisant des équipes pluridisciplinaires.
  • Vous pouvez justifier de contributions ou de succès significatifs dans le cadre d’initiatives business, au-delà d’en comprendre la logique ou les bonnes pratiques.
  • Votre capacité à nouer des relations de grande qualité avec des décideurs – Directions Générales, Directions Commerciales et B2B, Directions Marketing, Directions de la Transition Énergétique, Directions des Opérations ou DSI – fait de vous un acteur à l’aise et performant, de la découverte du besoin à la conclusion d’un deal équilibrant les intérêts du client et de WPP Enterprise Solutions.
  • Les enjeux des marchés B2B et du secteur de l’énergie vous passionnent, et vous savez vous appuyer sur vos expériences pour bâtir un discours solide en avant-vente comme en mission.
  • Votre rigueur et votre curiosité font de vous un acteur à la fois à l’aise dans la logique de développement business sur des clients existants que sur de la conquête opportuniste, ou en relai d’un partenaire.
  • La maîtrise de l’anglais, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, est indispensable : vous adressez des clients et des interlocuteurs internationaux de manière totalement autonome.

Intégrer WPP Enterprise Solutions, c’est choisir d’évoluer dans un environnement dynamique, humain et innovant, propice au développement de chacun, à la réalisation de missions enrichissantes et aux évolutions de carrière. description: Ben jij het zonnetje in huis? En heb jij al affiniteit met de wereld van bedrijfsovernames? Lees dan vooral verder! Wij zoeken namelijk een junior adviseur bedrijfsovernames. Je bent - samen met een senior collega - verantwoordelijk voor het gehele overnameproces van MKB bedrijven. Wat is je takenpakket? Je stelt anonieme overname profielen en informatiememoranda op en controleert ze Je spreekt met geïnteresseerden, nadat deze door je collega’s gekwalificeerd zijn Je voert onderhandelingsgesprekken met geïnteresseerden Je maakt de deal en het begeleidt het LOI-proces Je onderhoud korte lijnen met jouw klant (de ondernemer die zijn bedrijf gaat verkopen). Die voelt dat jij aan z’n kant staat. We hebben specialisten op elk gebied van het bedrijfsovernameproces; waardebepalingen, juridische afwikkeling en het informeren van geïnteresseerden. Dit is dus allemaal al geregeld en hoeft dus niet alles zelf te doen. Ondanks dat dit niet bij jouw verantwoordelijkheden hoort, krijg je hier wel alles van mee. We werken namelijk als een team. Mocht je ervaring en interesse hier liggen, dan kunnen we je takenpakket hiermee uitbreiden. Wie is onze ideale kandidaat? Je hebt affiniteit met overname processen Je communiceert op een natuurlijke en informele wijze met diverse partijen Je hebt affiniteit hebt met cijfers en je kunt uit de voeten met jaarrekeningen en financiële rapportages Je vind het leuk jezelf te verplaatsen in MKB ondernemers uit diverse sectoren en van allerlei niveau’s Je hebt overredingskracht en geeft tegengas aan je klant wanneer het nodig is Je hebt een winnaarsmentaliteit en gaat daarvoor graag “the extra mile” Je kunt gemakkelijk tussen cases schakelen: bij een fulltime dienstverband werk je doorgaans aan 10-15 cases tegelijkertijd Over Take 5 Over het algemeen zijn ondernemers ongeduldige mensen. Het liefst is alles gisteren al gebeurd. Wij kennen het overnameproces. We zijn hierin deskundig en ervaren. Dat wil zeggen: we hebben alle expertise in huis om een MKB’er zo goed mogelijk mee te nemen en we doen dit al een hele tijd. Het verkopen van een bedrijf doen MKB ondernemers maximaal 1-2 keer in hun leven. Ze staan hun kindje af. Dit is een emotioneel en spannend proces. Wij zijn toegewijd en pro-actief. We zijn streng op de kwalificatie en nemen alleen genoegen met het beste voor de ondernemer. We zijn authentiek en gelijkwaardig. Dat wil zeggen: we gaan naast een ondernemer staan en nemen die stap voor stap mee. We gebruiken ons karakter en eigenaardigheden om de connectie met de ondernemer te maken. Hoe lekkerder je zelf in je vel zit, hoe beter je iemand kunt helpen. Wat wij je bieden Een hecht team waar jouw werk direct zichtbaar impact heeft Een omgeving waar keihard werken en keihard lachen hand in hand gaat De ruimte om te mogen zijn wie je bent Veel verantwoordelijkheid en geen hiërarchisch gedoe Ruimte om te groeien in wat je nog niet kan maar wel wil leren Een werkomgeving waar ‘doen waar je energie van krijgt’ het aller-belangrijkste is Salaris en arbeidsvoorwaarden, daar komen we uit Belangrijk om te weten: voor deze functie zoeken we iemand die in loondienst komt. Daar tegenover staat dat je alle verantwoordelijkheden en voordelen krijgt die horen bij ondernemerschap. In de kern hebben wij geen programma om mede-eigenaar te worden. Mochten we er samen, na jarenlange gebleken geschiktheid, achter komen dat dit wel de juiste koers is, dan kan het alsnog. Dit is echter niet het initiële doel bij indiensttreding. Wat we zoeken Je hebt minimaal een HBO opleiding afgerond (de richting is niet zo belangrijk) Positiviteit en een drive om te winnen ⁠Je geeft zelfstandig gas, maar vindt samenwerken net zo belangrijk Je vindt het leuk om op een informele manier met veel verschillende ondernemers te schakelen Je bent empathisch en innemend Je hebt geen plankenkoorts Je bent in staat om minimaal 2 dagen per week te werken op ons kantoor in Bergen op Zoom Of je nu starter bent of ervaren: wie je bent is belangrijker dan wat je kunt. De wil om keihard gas te geven en dat met een enorme lach is het belangrijkst. Klaar om samen met ons op avontuur te gaan? Wil je samen met ons een van de belangrijkste stappen voor ondernemers waarmaken, en zelf óók groeien? Dan kunnen we niet wachten om van je te horen. Solliciteer met de knop op deze pagina. Zet je plankenkoorts maar aan de kant, want we doen het graag anders. Natuurlijk verwachten we echt geen Steven Spielberg kwaliteiten, maar blaas ons vooral omver met je persoonlijkheid Tot snel! description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people". The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build. How we build (worth reading before the role) How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next. We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be. We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out. About the role So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role. You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value. Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer. That's also what makes it exciting. You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together. Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business. Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product". Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join. What matters most We need all of these at once: Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up. Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea. Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked. Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see. Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features. Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's. And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code. What you'll actually do Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it. Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution. Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense. Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built. Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst. Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck. About you You'll likely thrive here if: You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention. You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line. You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself. Nice-to-haves: You were a software engineer before you moved into product. You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces. You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off. This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned. How we work We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you. Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first. We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it. Remuneration and benefits Compelling package including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough to pay real salaries, and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together. 🏢 A great office set up for collaborative work (we already need more whiteboards) 💻 The equipment, setup and training you need to do your best work 🤝 A high-context environment with real exposure to the big decisions, in the room when it happens ☕ Very good coffee 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month ✈️ 33 days paid holiday (including bank holidays) 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway. Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, Agentic SDLC - (EMEA Only)

An overview of this role

GitLab’s Forward Deployed Engineering team is a field-situated product engineering function focused on strategic customer outcomes, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and direct contributions to GitLab’s product. This isn't a traditional field engineering, solutions architecture, or professional services role. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work closely with customers while maintaining the technical standards and contribution discipline of a Staff-level product engineer.

You'll work where strategic customer urgency, complex technical ambiguity, and GitLab product execution intersect. You'll partner directly with strategic customers and teams across Product, Engineering, Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Solutions Architecture (SA), Customer Success Architecture (CSA), Customer Success Management (CSM), and Professional Services. You'll diagnose and resolve high-impact adoption blockers, contribute production-quality fixes and features, and turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for GitLab and its customers.

Why this role exists

Strategic customers sometimes encounter challenges that are too broad, deep, urgent, or cross-functional for any single team to own from start to finish. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability.

Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. The team doesn't simply observe, report, or escalate. You'll engage directly, diagnose the underlying technical problem, collaborate with the right teams, contribute code or technical solutions where appropriate, and transition the outcome into normal ownership once the customer is stable and the learning can be reused.

What you’ll do

Product contribution

  • Contribute production-quality code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering work.
  • Work within GitLab’s product and engineering processes, including issue discovery, merge request creation, testing, review, documentation, and maintainability.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering so customer-driven solutions support long-term product direction rather than becoming one-off customizations.
  • Turn blockers discovered in the field into durable product improvements, reference architectures, documentation, and repeatable implementation patterns.

Strategic technical stewardship

  • Engage with strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.
  • Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments.
  • Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and customer technical teams to drive resolution from discovery through handoff.
  • Provide recommendations grounded in data, traces, and systems analysis to improve GitLab usage, workflows, automation, and architecture.
  • Create durable outcomes without establishing permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.

AI adoption and agentic software development lifecycle

  • Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.
  • Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.
  • Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.

Thought leadership

  • Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.
  • Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.
  • Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.
  • Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.

What you’ll bring

  • Staff-level experience building, operating, or improving complex production software systems.
  • Experience contributing to large, mature product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.
  • Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.
  • Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.
  • Deep knowledge of modern DevSecOps workflows, including Git, merge requests, CI/CD, security controls, compliance needs, and enterprise software delivery.
  • Experience working with strategic customers or senior technical stakeholders in ambiguous, high-impact situations.
  • The ability to coordinate across product, engineering, field, and customer teams without formal authority.
  • Strong written communication and sound judgment, including the ability to create technical narratives and distinguish reusable product work from customer-specific customization.

Strongly preferred qualifications

  • Direct experience with GitLab as a platform, including GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, or GitLab Self-Managed.
  • Production experience with Ruby on Rails, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, Vue, TypeScript, Kubernetes, Docker, Linux, or observability tools.
  • Deep familiarity with Git internals, repository performance, large-scale Git usage patterns, or GitLab Runner behavior.
  • Experience creating technical thought-leadership materials, such as whitepapers, technical talks, architecture frameworks, requests for comments, public technical writing, or internal strategy documents.

Technologies and domains

  • Go

  • PostgreSQL

What this role is not

This role isn't:

description:
About CAIS
CAIS is the pioneer in democratizing access to and education about alternative investments for independent financial advisors, empowering them to engage and transact with leading asset managers on a massive scale through a wide variety of alternative investment products and technology solutions. CAIS provides financial advisors with a broad selection of alternative investment strategies, including hedge funds, private equity, private credit, real estate, digital assets, and structured notes. CAIS also delivers industry-leading technology, operational efficiency, and world-class client service throughout the pre-trade, trade, and post-trade experience. CAIS serves over 2,500 wealth management firms that support more than 65,000 financial advisors who oversee approximately $8.5 trillion in end-client assets. 

About the role
We’re looking for a Senior Backend Product Engineer to join our Capital Markets technology team in London. This is a hybrid, hands-on role: you’ll design, build and run systems across Pre-Trade, Trade and Post-Trade, covering Structured Investments, Equity IPOs, Hedging & Monetization, ETFs, and more. 

We put a lot of emphasis on the “product” in product engineer. You’ll work alongside product managers and directly with the business to turn open-ended problems into working software, and the results show up in how a fast-growing company performs. AI is a big part of how we work: the team uses it throughout the development lifecycle and has already shipped several agentic features. You’ll help build the next ones. 

We work in small, autonomous teams using the Kanban principles of optimizing flow and limiting WIP. The team owns its work together, from shaping the problem through to running it in production. We collaborate closely with colleagues and stakeholders in New York. Engineers own their work from shaping the problem through to running it in production. While we have access to QA expertise, we consider quality to be everyone’s responsibility, so engineers own testing too. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, especially as AI changes how we build. 

You’ll mostly write Kotlin, working with Spring, Postgres, Elasticsearch and Kafka, and deploying to Kubernetes on AWS through GitHub and ArgoCD. 

Why join us 

  • Real ownership: you’ll shape problems with the business, not just pick up tickets 
  • Visible impact: your work shows up directly in how a fast-growing business performs 
  • Interesting domain: complex, real-world problems across the full trade lifecycle 
  • Engineering quality: strong fundamentals and high standards 
  • Modern codebase: we’ve moved off legacy, and our systems have been built in the last few years 

Skills & Experience 

  • Experience working as a software developer with Java or Kotlin server-side applications 
  • Track record of turning business problems into working software, with a clear, measurable impact 
  • Experience building and running mission-critical services in production, from CI/CD through to monitoring, alerting and incident response 
  • Strong testing habits across unit, integration and end-to-end tests, with good judgment about what to test at each level
  • Strong experience with Spring (Boot, Data, Security), relational database design, REST API design, and Kafka or a similar event streaming platform 
  • Experience working AI-first: using AI agents to build software, with an understanding of how LLMs work and good judgement about when to trust their output 
  • Technical leadership within your team, including mentoring less experienced engineers and setting and sharing engineering standards 
  • Clear communication, including explaining technical decisions to non-engineers 

Nice to have 

  • Financial services experience, ideally capital markets 
  • Elasticsearch, Kubernetes, Postgres, AWS, Terraform 
  • TypeScript and React, and/or motivation to try full stack development 
  • Experience building AI or agentic applications 

This role is a hybrid role, with at least 2-3 days spent out of our Old Street office - N1 7LB. 

CAIS is consistently recognized as a Best Place to Work, and our culture is at the heart of our success. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where employees can be their most authentic self and feel inspired and supported to bring their voice forward to drive community, growth, and innovation. We are an equal opportunity employer, and do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law.  Learn more about our culture, benefits, and people at https://www.caisgroup.com/our-company/careers.

description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Senior Category Manager, Home (EU Country)

We are seeking a Senior Category Manager, Home EU to join our growing team. This role owns the end-to-end product strategy for designated Home categories, with full accountability for assortment, launches, revenue, margins, and long-term category growth. In this role, you will play a critical part in scaling Quince’s value proposition in the EU by building a compelling, high-quality assortment that delights customers while delivering strong business results.

Responsibilities

  • Own all end-to-end product strategy and assortment for designated Home categories in the EU, including category strategy, assortment, launches, and performance.
  • Category-expert, sets long-term strategy with support; may build department from the ground up, with oversight.
  • Partner with Marketing to develop and lead the go-to-market strategy and execution for these categories in the EU 
  • Partner with Supply Chain and Sourcing to maximize margin for category in the EU
  • Analyze data to drive decision-making, including sales velocity, margin, return rate, etc.
  • Collaborate with key cross-functional partners, particularly Design, Creative, Planning, and Marketing, to ensure we are developing products that meet our brand/style requirements, we are maintaining in-stock position, and are driving traffic to key products.
  • Leveraging data for ratings, reviews, and return rates, participate and spearhead quality improvements for any products in assortment with improvement opportunities.
  • Assist in onboarding additional best-in-class vendors to the Quince model to expand source base.
  • Continuously identify whitespace in the assortment and refine product roadmap based on new information and learnings.
  • Build site merchandising strategy, including PDP improvements roadmap and top nav and filter optimizations.

Qualifications

Required

  • 8-10 years of retail merchandising or buying experience in home categories, with demonstrated ownership of category performance. 
  • E-commerce experience and/or DTC experience preferred
  • Proven track record of progressing within an organization and demonstrating continuous growth in roles and responsibilities
  • Product obsessed with experience in leveraging data tools and external sources
  • Critical eye to anticipate customer needs (both the “science” and “art” of retail merchandising)
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and execution-focused, with a demonstrated ability for building scalable processes and driving cross-functional alignment
  • Continuous learner and highly curious; always open to considering new perspectives; proactive when changing course and facing added challenges
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • Motivated by working in a fast-paced collaborative environment, where flexibility to stretch into or out of functional comfort zones is crucial for team success
  • Bachelor’s Degree, preferred
  • Role is based in one of our UK/EU (London, Madrid, or Berlin) offices, with 4 days per week (Monday-Thursday) in office requirement.

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.
